messages.subject: Doubly stochastic mixture model
parts:
Hi folks,

I'm trying to evaluate the parameters of a doubly stocastic mixture model, where one of the mixture components' pdf has a parameter that has it's own pdf. Below my signature I've pasted an example, including fake-data-generation for clarity on what I mean by the previous sentence :Op. 

When I run the model, I get the warning and error pasted below the code (the message under "Error:" actually repeats many times, and no samples are actually taken). I'm sure I'm just making a simple conceptual error in how to implement this. Any help would be greatly appreciated!

Mike



########
# Generate some fake data
########
gamma_mean = 10
gamma_scale = 20
rho = .8

#convert to rgamma parameterization
gamma_shape = gamma_mean*(1/gamma_scale)

#loop to generate data
y = rep(NA,1e3)
for(i in 1:length(y)){
if(runif(1)<=rho){
kappa = rgamma(1,shape=gamma_shape,scale=gamma_scale)
y[i] = rvm(1,mean=pi,k=kappa)
}else{
y[i] = runif(1,0,2*pi)
}
}

#check what it looks like
hist(y,br=100)

#check qqplot against von mises (should have a kink in the tails and near the middle)
qqplot(y,rvm(1e3,pi,gamma_mean))

#package data for stan
data_for_stan = list(
data_count = length(y)
, y = y
)

#define the stan model
model_code = "
data {
int<lower=0> data_count ;
real<lower=0,upper=2*pi()> y[data_count] ;
}
transformed data{
real neglog2pi;
neglog2pi <- -log(2.0 * pi()); #log-probability of uniform component (i.e. data invariant)
}
parameters {
real<lower=0,upper=1> rho ;
real<lower=0> gamma_mean ;
real<lower=0> gamma_scale ;
}
model {
//initialize some local variables
real ps[2] ;
real this_kappa ;
 
//set priors on population parameters
rho ~ uniform(0,1);
gamma_mean ~ cauchy(0,50);
gamma_scale ~ cauchy(0,50);
//iterate through the data, updating the log-probability
for (i in 1:data_count){
this_kappa ~ gamma(gamma_mean*(1/gamma_scale),1/gamma_scale) ;
if (this_kappa<10){ //to avoid overflow error caused by high values of kappa
ps[1] <- log(rho) + von_mises_log(y[i],pi(),this_kappa) ;
}else{
ps[1] <- log(rho) + normal_log(y[i],pi(),sqrt(1/this_kappa)) ;
}
ps[2] <- log(1-rho) + neglog2pi ;
increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(ps)) ;
}
}
"


########
# Evaluate the model
########
set_cppo(mode = 'debug') #set the compiler mode to "debug" for initial testing, then "fast" for fitting

#pre-compile the model
fit <- stan(
model_code = model_code
, data = data_for_stan
, iter = 1e2
, chains = 1
)

parts: oh, and this_kappa needed to be not a single value but of length "data_count" and the sampling statement involving "this_kappa" needed to be pulled out of the for loop. for posterity, here is the working model code:

data {
int<lower=0> data_count ;
real<lower=0,upper=2*pi()> y[data_count] ;
}
transformed data{
real neglog2pi;
neglog2pi <- -log(2.0 * pi()); #log-probability of uniform component (i.e. data invariant)
}
parameters {
real<lower=0,upper=1> rho ;
real<lower=0> gamma_mean ;
real<lower=0> gamma_scale ;
real<lower=0> this_kappa[data_count] ;

}
model {
//initialize some local variables
real ps[2] ;

//set priors on population parameters
rho ~ uniform(0,1);
gamma_mean ~ cauchy(0,50);
gamma_scale ~ cauchy(0,50);

//iterate through the data, updating the log-probability
for (i in 1:data_count){

if (this_kappa[i]<10){ //to avoid overflow error caused by high values of kappa
ps[1] <- log(rho) + von_mises_log(y[i],pi(),this_kappa[i]) ;
}else{
ps[1] <- log(rho) + normal_log(y[i],pi(),sqrt(1/this_kappa[i])) ;

}
ps[2] <- log(1-rho) + neglog2pi ;
increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(ps)) ;
}
}
